title: Phase calibration unlocks adaptive tests for renewed quantum noise
abstract: Can interventions distinguish an unknown phase that is frozen throughout an experiment from phase noise renewed at every use? We study ordinary forward queries, arbitrary quantum memory, and exactly zero false positives for every frozen diagonal unitary. For any Schur channel with correlation matrix C, the optimal parallel failure probability is min over occupation vectors m of per(C[m])/n!. The same formula is the exact optimum over all causal strategies when the renewed channel has an unknown common phase carrier and failure is evaluated in the worst case over that carrier. Calibration changes this conclusion: for qubit dephasing we give a rational five-query certificate that beats every parallel strategy for 0.5331424052... < eta < 1. At eta=0.7, failure decreases from 0.46603 to 0.4602957928558. We prove physical realizability of the certificate, obtain exact causal limits at complete dephasing, and show that adaptation cannot improve the asymptotic failure exponent. The separation concerns finite-query performance under a calibrated statistical promise; it neither quantifies the hardware cost of a phase reference nor certifies a quantum environment.
